title: Yellow Spicy Malaysian Pork Tenderloin Satay
description: A spicy and juicy Malaysian dish featuring pork tenderloin, served in a romantic and ayurvedic-sattvic-friendly way, shaped like nigiri.
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat, about 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a blender or food processor, combine coconut milk, curry powder, turmeric, cumin, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper, and blend until smooth.
Place the pork tenderloin in a large ziplock bag, and pour the coconut milk mixture over it, turning to coat evenly.
Seal the bag, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight, turning occasionally.
Remove the pork from the marinade, and thread onto skewers, if desired, shaping like nigiri.
Grill the pork for 12-15 minutes, turning occasionally, until it reaches an internal temperature of 145 degrees Fahrenheit.
Let the pork rest for 5 minutes before slicing thinly.
Serve the pork with a squeeze of lemon juice, and garnished with chopped fresh cilantro.
Offer with steamed vegetables or rice for a complete meal.
